## Summary

There is a high severity authentication vulnerability in Traefik's ForwardAuth middleware when the authentication server uses a connection-bound scheme such as NTLM or SPNEGO/Kerberos "Negotiate" (for example IIS Windows Authentication). ForwardAuth sends its authentication subrequests through a connection pool shared by every client of the middleware, so an auth-server connection already authenticated by one user can be reused for the subrequest of an unrelated client. An unauthenticated client on a separate frontend connection can then receive a successful authentication response carrying the victim's identity, which Traefik forwards to the backend through `authResponseHeaders`, and access the backend as that user. In Traefik v3.7 the same applies to the external authentication requests issued for the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider's `auth-url` annotation.

This is a distinct issue from GHSA-53qr-784g-cj35, GHSA-qqjf-53cj-pwvv, GHSA-cw35-4q88-3rmp and GHSA-qm9f-w54v-q2qh, which isolated connection-bound authentication on the backend proxy paths only; the fix applies the same per-frontend-connection isolation to the authentication server. Traefik v3.0 through v3.6 are end-of-life and are also affected; they will not receive a fix on their own line, and users on those versions must upgrade to v2.11.60 or v3.7.16.

## Patches
